what: The Percentage Calculator answers the three most common percent questions in one place: what is X% of a number, what percent one number is of another, and the percentage change from one number to another. Each question has its own small section, so you can use them separately.

It helps students with homework, shoppers with discounts, workers with pay rises, and anyone reading reports or statistics. You do not need to remember which number to divide by which; the labels guide you.
Results appear as you type, and everything runs in your browser.
uses: Find a share of a number
Work out 15% of 200, a tip, a commission or a tax amount.
Turn a score into a percent
Find what percent 42 out of 50 marks is.
See the percentage increase in sales, prices or visitors.
See the percentage decrease when a price or number goes down.
Compare an old and new price to find the real discount.
tutorial: In "What is X% of Y?", type the percent in "Percent (%)" and the number in "Of number". The answer appears in the box below.
Find what percent X is of Y
In "X is what percent of Y?", type the part in "Number X" and the whole in "Number Y". The answer is shown with a % sign. Y cannot be 0.
In "Percentage change from X to Y", type the old value in "From" and the new value in "To". The result says how many percent and whether it is an "increase" or "decrease".
Each section works by itself. You only need to fill in the two boxes of the section you want.
All boxes accept decimals and negative numbers, such as -5 or 12.75.
features: X as a percent of Y
Change = (To − From) ÷ From × 100, using the size of From, so negative starting values work too. The result is labeled increase, decrease or no change.
You see "Y cannot be zero" or "Starting value cannot be zero" instead of a wrong answer.
Answers are shown with up to 2 decimals.
No switching between pages for different percent questions.

example.title: Worked example: three percent questions
example.text: What is 15% of 200? Type 15 and 200 and you get 30, because 15 ÷ 100 × 200 = 30. What percent is 30 of 200? Type 30 and 200 and you get 15%. A price went from 80 to 100: type 80 in "From" and 100 in "To" and the result is "25% increase", because (100 − 80) ÷ 80 × 100 = 25. Going back from 100 to 80 gives "20% decrease", which shows that a rise and a fall of the same amount are not the same percent.

tips: In percentage change, always put the old value in "From" and the new one in "To".
A 25% increase followed by a 20% decrease brings you back to the start.
To find a discount percent, put the original price in "From" and the sale price in "To".
For exam marks, put your score in "Number X" and the maximum in "Number Y".
Results are rounded to 2 decimals; 1 of 3 shows as 33.33%.
problems: You cannot find a percent of 0. Enter a non-zero whole in "Number Y".
It says "Starting value cannot be zero"
Percentage change from 0 is not defined. Use a non-zero "From" value.
Both boxes in that section must be filled in.
The change says decrease but I expected increase
Check that the old value is in "From" and the new value is in "To".
